title: Observability: multi-tenant sampling hierarchies and resilient pipeline fanout for Dedicated/VPC
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private deployments produce high-volume telemetry from many tenants and GPU pools. The current collector fanout and sampling are flat: either we drop too many spans for high-volume tenants (loss of signal for latency debugging) or we forward everything (overloads downstream pipelines and increases egress costs). We also lack a tracing hook that lets the runtime mark spans with SLA-aware priority (e.g., real-time inference vs. background batch warmups).

Goal: Implement a hierarchical, tenant-aware sampling and fanout pipeline that preserves high-fidelity traces for SLA-sensitive traffic while gracefully shedding unneeded telemetry from noisy tenants. Add tracing hook primitives in the serving runtime so spans are annotated with priority and workload_class. Provide resilient fanout logic in the VPC/on-prem forwarder that supports back-pressure, offline buffering, and per-tenant routing to isolated ingest pipelines.

Why this matters: Customers on Dedicated and Private care deeply about being able to debug latency and SLO regressions without exposing sensitive tenant telemetry or paying for unnecessary egress. This work reduces mean time to resolution for perf incidents, keeps observability costs predictable under load, and improves isolation between tenants on shared gateways.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes tracing hook API: annotate_span(priority=<high|medium|low>, workload_class=<inference|kv-cache|batch>)
Collector forwards priority=high spans immediately to a priority queue and ensures delivery under normal backpressure
Sampler config supports per-tenant sampling hierarchy: guaranteed N traces/hour for customers with SLA flag, reservoir sampling for medium priority, aggressive tail-drop for low priority
Fanout component supports dynamic target list updates and hides downstream failures (exponential backoff + disk-backed buffer)
End-to-end test shows <1% loss of high-priority spans during a 3x ingestion spike and no more than 5% tail increase in P99 latency for trace ingestion
New Dashboard: Dedicated Observability -> Latency & Errors by Capacity Pool shows priority-filtered heatmaps and tenant-slice drilldown
Docs updated with API examples and migration notes for Dedicated/Private customers
design_notes: Introduce a small runtime SDK surface: hook_register('observability.priority', returns token) and span_set_token(span, token). Minimal overhead in hot path (~<0.5% CPU).

Sampling model: tiered reservoir sampler. Top-tier (SLA) gets guaranteed reservoir quota; mid-tier uses adaptive rate estimated from recent RPS and error budgets; bottom-tier uses probabilistic tail-sampler keyed by trace fingerprint to preserve outliers.

Forwarder: replace synchronous fanout with an async dispatcher that maintains per-target queues. Implement back-pressure signals: when downstream indicates saturation, move targets into exponential backoff and drain to disk-backed buffer (with tenant-scoped eviction policy).
Security: tenant metadata never sent to shared telemetry backends unless explicitly allowed by customer config. Use tenant-scoped encryption keys for on-disk buffers in on-prem deployments.

Compatibility: Support two modes for on-prem collectors: shim-mode (sidecar present) and shimless (agent baked into runtime). Provide migration path and feature flags to toggle sampling hierarchy per cluster.
Metrics: expose counters for sampling decisions, buffer sizes per-tenant, fanout backoff count, and lost-span counts. Tag metrics by capacity_pool and tenant_id hash (not raw id) to avoid PII leaks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable runtime tracing hook and collector fanout changes in internal Dedicated cluster. Route 1% of tenants (non-prod) through new pipeline. Observe latency and span delivery metrics for 72h.
Phase 2 (limited customer opt-in): Offer to 3 external beta customers on Dedicated. Provide migration checklist and opt-in flag in Console. Run beta for 2 weeks under load tests.

Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Automate per-pool rollout with 10% increments. Monitor priority-span loss and ingress pipeline lag. Abort conditions: >2% loss of high-priority spans for 1h or >3x increase in ingress P99 latency.
Phase 4 (GA): Flip defaults for Dedicated runtime images and update on-prem agent package. Publish docs and SDK examples.
test_plan: Unit tests for reservoir sampler behavior across edge cases (burst, drop, steady-state)
Integration test: synthetic generator creating mixed workloads (SLA-sensitive inference, background warmups, batch jobs) verifies sampling tiers preserve expected quotas
Chaos test: kill downstream ingest endpoints to validate disk-backed buffer durability and recovery without data corruption
Performance: benchmark runtime hook overhead at 0, 10k, 50k req/s and ensure <1% CPU overhead at 50k req/s
E2E validation: run long-running soak (48h) with tenant skew and confirm dashboards accurately reflect latency and error distributions per priority
